images.author: Harry Rose from South West Rocks, Australia (posted to Flickr by Macleay Grass Man)
images.attribution: "Taraxacum officinale leaf1" by Harry Rose (Macleay Grass Man on Flickr), licensed CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Taraxacum_officinale_leaf1_(16189363040).jpg
images.changesNote: Changes made, and must be stated: resized (from Wikimedia's 960px rendition of the 4000x3000 original) to 640x480 and re-encoded as WebP at quality 85. No crop and no colour edit.
images.shows: One upright, deeply toothed, smooth-looking leaf with its teeth pointing back toward the base, photographed against grass.
images.doesNotShow: A whole rosette: this is a single leaf, not the rosette. Leaf hairlessness is consistent with the image but a 640px photograph cannot establish it.

images.author: Dcrjsr
images.attribution: "Common dandelion Taraxacum officinale flowers" by Dcrjsr, licensed CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Common_dandelion_Taraxacum_officinale_flowers.jpg
images.changesNote: Changes made, and must be stated: resized (from Wikimedia's 960px rendition of the 5472x3648 original) to 560x373 and re-encoded as WebP at quality 58. No crop and no colour edit.
images.shows: About ten open yellow heads, each made of many ray florets with no central disc of a different kind, among deeply cut basal leaves on bare soil.
images.doesNotShow: A close-up of one head. At 560px each head is roughly 30 to 50 px across, so bracts beneath the head are not visible.

images.shows: Four to five leafless, unbranched stalks each carrying a single head, rising from a low clump of leaves against a brick wall.
images.doesNotShow: Whether the stalks are hollow. Other small plants (white-flowered) share the frame. The photographer's own caption says 'June 2007. I think.' about the date.

images.shows: Thin, wiry flowering stalks with visible forks: at least one stalk splits into two branches each ending in a bud, and the stalk carrying the one open flower also has a bud beside it. One open yellow head with a small insect on it.
images.doesNotShow: Leaf hairiness (no leaves in frame). The species identification is the uploader's.

images.shows: The underside of one pale leaf held between a thumb and finger, with fine bristle-like hairs visible along the margin and midrib, against moss and litter.
images.doesNotShow: A rosette, and it is not a leaf of dandelion for comparison. The leaf is pale yellow-green rather than 'dark green' (a colour the Penn State page mentions). Hairs are small at 640px.
